full_judgment:
8. He also submits that though the accused was arrested after almost 10 years of the occurrence and the present proceeding was filed in 1999 but provision of section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay of any days in preferring a Criminal appeal against the conviction and sentence was also applicable. So, the convict petitioner cannot file a petition under section 561A of the Code for setting aside the conviction and sentence imposed upon him by a Sessions Judge. So, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 11. But in our opinion when there is a clear provision of appeal against the judgment of conviction and sentence of the Sessions Judge and the Additional Sessions Judge under section 410 of the Code and since the provision of section 5 of the Limitation Act is also applicable therein, as such, there was no any legal scope for the convict petitioner to prefer a petition for quashing the proceeding against his conviction and sentence. Since there is efficacious relief in preferring the appeal with a prayer for condonation of delays of any day under section 5 of the Limitation Act, the very filing of a petition under section 561A of the Code for quashing the conviction and sentence of the petitioner passed by Sessions Judge is not at all maintainable. 

 12. In our consideration the very filing of a petition under section 561A of the Code for quashing the conviction and sentence passed by a Sessions Judge where there is specific provision of application of section 5 of the Limitation Act the very continuation of such a proceeding is the abuse of the process of the Court. So, we find it difficult to discuss any more in this Rule since the Rule is not itself maintainable.
